title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status. RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral. CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited. METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression. RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68). DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: High-intensity focused ultrasound as a bridging vascular-modulating therapy for fertility-sparing management of placental site trophoblastic tumor complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) is a rare gestational trophoblastic neoplasm characterized by local invasiveness and marked vascularity. Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old woman presented with persistently plateaued serum human chorionic gonadotropin levels following hysteroscopic management for suspected incomplete abortion. Imaging revealed a deeply invasive hypervascular uterine lesion with UAVF, raising strong suspicion of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Given her strong desire for fertility preservation and high surgical risk, ultrasound-guided HIFU was performed as an initial vascular-modulating intervention. Subsequent expert pathological review confirmed PSTT. RESULTS: HIFU achieved significant reduction in lesion perfusion and vascular flow, as confirmed by Doppler ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI. Although complete tumor ablation was not achieved due to lesion size and deep invasion, subsequent low-dose chemotherapy resulted in complete biochemical remission accompanied by radiologic regression of residual lesions. No major HIFU-related complications were observed, and normal menstrual function resumed during follow-up. CONCLUSION: HIFU is a technically feasible and safe fertility-preserving adjunct for vascular modulation in hypervascular PSTT complicated by UAVF. While HIFU alone may not achieve definitive oncologic control in large or deeply invasive lesions, it can serve as a bridging strategy to reduce tumor perfusion and vascularity, facilitating subsequent systemic therapy in carefully selected patients. This approach demonstrates the potential role of HIFU as a bridging vascular-modulating strategy within multimodal fertility-preserving management.

title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Management of Brachial Plexus Neurogenic Tumors: A Retrospective Study of 25 Cases.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To investigate the clinical characteristics of cervical brachial plexus neurogenic tumors and enhance the diagnostic and therapeutic management of this condition. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 25 patients diagnosed with brachial plexus neurogenic tumors who were treated at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations, treatment strategies, and follow-up outcomes were systematically summarized. RESULTS: A total of 25 patients were included, treated across multiple departments: otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedics, thyroid surgery, and vascular surgery. There were 13 male and 12 female patients, aged 16-76 y, with a disease duration ranging from 1 wk to 2 y, defined as the interval from symptom onset to initial clinical evaluation. The primary presenting symptom was a neck root mass in 21 patients, among whom seven experienced ipsilateral upper limb numbness, soreness, or electric shock-like pain upon palpation and four reported sensory disturbances in the upper extremity or shoulder-back pain. All patients underwent cervical contrast-enhanced computed tomography, and 18 additionally received 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging. Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration cytology was performed in all cases, revealing spindle cell tumors with morphological features suggestive of schwannoma. Of the 25 patients, 23 underwent surgical resection, while two with small tumors (<2 cm), no neurological symptoms, and cytologically benign findings opted for conservative management with close observation. Surgical approaches included the anterior supraclavicular approach, the posterior cervical paravertebral approach, and clavicle-splitting (transclavicular) approach. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed benign schwannoma in 22 cases and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor in one case. Follow-up duration ranged from 12 to 60 mo. Transient postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in five patients, manifesting as limited shoulder abduction, reduced wrist extensor strength, or limb numbness; all deficits resolved within 6 mo following structured rehabilitation programs. CONCLUSIONS: Brachial plexus neurogenic tumors commonly present as a mass in the neck root, with a subset of cases accompanied by neurological symptoms. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are valuable modalities for tumor localization and qualitative characterization. Preoperative fine needle aspiration cytology enables a preliminary assessment of tumor histology. The selection of an appropriate surgical approach should be guided by tumor location and anatomical involvement. Intralesional enucleation is a key strategy for preserving neurological function, and when combined with microsurgical techniques and intraoperative nerve monitoring, even transient postoperative neurological deficits can be effectively managed through structured rehabilitation programs.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: Self-assembled, carrier-free cyclic chemerin 9/tannic acid coating for enhanced vascular healing following stent deployment.
abstract: Endovascular stent implantation has gained traction as a critical therapeutic strategy for managing cerebral atherosclerotic stenosis and preventing acute ischaemic stroke. Although bare-metal stents (BMSs) are widely used in clinical applications, their therapeutic efficacy is limited by in-stent restenosis (ISR). Drug-eluting stents (DESs) have been developed to inhibit ISR and have demonstrated satisfactory short-term clinical results. However, the non-specific cytotoxicity of the eluted drugs on endothelial cells impairs re-endothelialisation, thereby increasing the risk of ISR and stent thrombosis at a late stage. In addition, the residual polymer carriers and coupling agents can induce persistent hypersensitivity reactions and inflammation. Herein, we developed an anti-inflammatory, endothelium-compatible stent. The tannic acid (TA)/cyclic chemerin 9 (C9)-modified stent was fabricated via a layer-by-layer (LBL) self-assembly method, leveraging noncovalent interactions between the anti-inflammatory peptide cyclic C9 and polyphenol TA. This stent was constructed without polymer carriers or coupling agents. The TA and C9 released from the TA/C9-modified stent synergistically attenuated inflammatory cascades and repressed smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration, and exerted no adverse effect on endothelial cell coverage. This design effectively eliminates chronic inflammation associated with residual carriers and coupling agents. In a porcine model, the TA/C9-modified stent demonstrated superior efficacy in enhancing vascular healing and suppressing neointimal hyperplasia. These results indicate that the TA/C9-modified stent represents a promising strategy for improving long-term outcomes in cerebrovascular stent design.

title: Association of limb fat distribution and plasma metabolites with the risk of venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a potentially life-threatening cardiovascular condition. However, the role of limb-specific fat distribution and its associated metabolomic signatures in VTE remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To assess associations between upper- and lower-limb fat distribution and VTE risk and to evaluate whether circulating metabolites mediate these relationships. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed UK Biobank data, in which arm and leg fat mass were measured by bioelectrical impedance. Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines assessed sex-specific associations with incident VTE, deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used to identify metabolites associated with arm-to-leg fat mass percentage, followed by mediation analyses. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.6 years, 14 593 VTE events occurred among 458 651 participants. A higher arm-to-leg fat mass percentage was associated with increased VTE risk, with hazard ratios of 1.81 (95% CI, 1.63-2.00) in women and 1.55 (95% CI, 1.47-1.64) in men when comparing the highest tertile with the lowest. A total of 138 metabolites in women and 38 in men were associated with arm-to-leg fat distribution. In women, the metabolomic signature mediated 15.2% (95% CI, 6.8%-21.9%) of the association between arm-to-leg fat and VTE and 21.1% (95% CI, 12.8%-28.4%) of the corresponding association with pulmonary embolism; no significant mediation was observed in men. CONCLUSION: Predominant upper peripheral fat distribution is associated with a high risk of VTE. Sex-specific metabolomic signatures partially mediate these associations in women, underscoring the importance of integrating limb fat distribution with metabolomics to improve VTE risk assessment.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Noninvasive Repair of Arteriovenous Fistula Stenosis Using Xilang Loubao Combined with Standardized Traditional Chinese Medicine Nursing Massage: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis threatens long-term dialysis access viability. Invasive interventions carry risks of trauma and recurrence, creating a clinical need for safe noninvasive adjunct care options. This trial evaluated a nurse-led protocol combining Xilang Loubao (a food-grade bioactive peptide formulation) with standardized traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) nursing massage for AVF maintenance, with Doppler ultrasound supporting real-time nursing assessment. METHODS: From January to June 2025, a total of 82 outpatients with AVF stenosis from Liaoyuan Central Hospital were recruited and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to 2 groups of 41 patients each. The experimental group received Xilang Loubao plus TCM nursing massage, with 1 withdrawal, leaving 40 completers. The control group used mucopolysaccharide polysulfate cream plus routine care, with 6 withdrawals, leaving 35 completers. The primary end point was 90-day change in AVF stenotic diameter measured by Doppler, and the secondary end points included hemodynamics and nursing-related adverse events. RESULTS: At baseline, groups were comparable in age, vessel diameter, and blood flow. By Day 90, the intervention group had mean AVF stenotic-site diameter 4.3 ± 0.7 mm and brachial artery flow 1086.6 ± 253.5 mL/min, while controls were 2.0 ± 0.4 mm and 482.9 ± 123.1 mL/min (all P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Under color Doppler ultrasound guidance, this nurse-led combined nursing approach showed potential to improve with good safety, serving as an adjunct nursing option to help prolong AVF patency in patients with AVF stenosis.

title: Three decades of Rex shunt for pediatric extrahepatic portal vein obstruction: A narrative review of advances from surgical evolution to holistic management.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Since its introduction in 1992, the Rex shunt (also called Meso-Rex bypass, MRB) has substantially advanced the management of pediatric extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO) by restoring physiological hepatopetal portal flow. However, a comprehensive synthesis of the accumulating evidence and evolving practices is notably lacking, especially given that the latest Baveno VI consensus was published nine years ago in 2016. OBJECTIVE: This review aims to synthesize three decades of advances in Rex shunt evolution, from a novel technique to a widely adopted first-line surgical option. METHODS: We conducted a narrative review, synthesizing evidence from key studies, large case series, and expert consensus statements. RESULTS: Key topics addressed include the comparison between Rex shunt and portosystemic shunts, evolving surgical indications, technical evolution of the procedure, critical aspects of perioperative management, identification of prognostic factors, and management of vascular complications. The review highlights the superior potential of the Rex shunt in resolving the sequelae of EHPVO and outlines the importance of a holistic management approach. CONCLUSION: The Rex shunt represents a major advance in the management of pediatric EHPVO. Optimal outcomes depend on careful patient selection, meticulous surgical technique, and comprehensive perioperative care, supported by an experienced multidisciplinary team.

title: Hemodynamic Differences Associated with Extreme Versus Minimal Proximal Neck Angulation in Ruptured Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Patient-Specific Computational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maximum aneurysm diameter remains the principal criterion for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) risk assessment, but additional morphologic and biomechanical factors may help explain the heterogeneity of rupture-related vulnerability. This exploratory study aimed to characterize hemodynamic differences associated with extreme versus minimal proximal neck angulation in ruptured infrarenal AAAs. METHODS: Preoperative computed tomography angiography datasets from six patients with ruptured infrarenal AAAs were retrospectively analyzed. Cases were categorized into an extreme angulation group (70° < β < 90°, n = 3) and a minimal angulation group (β < 5°, n = 3). Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics models were reconstructed to compare intrasac flow pattern, wall pressure distribution, and wall shear stress (WSS). RESULTS: Compared with minimal angulation, extreme proximal neck angulation was associated with more disturbed intrasac flow, greater flow acceleration at the neck-sac junction, and more heterogeneous wall pressure and WSS distributions. Minimally angulated aneurysms showed relatively laminar flow, whereas severely angulated aneurysms demonstrated more prominent recirculation and flow disorder. Regions of abnormal hemodynamic behavior showed qualitative spatial concordance with clinically identified rupture sites. CONCLUSION: In this small exploratory series of ruptured infrarenal AAAs, extreme proximal neck angulation was associated with a more adverse intrasac hemodynamic environment than minimal angulation. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating, do not establish reproducible hemodynamic patterns or rupture risk prediction, and require validation in larger, preferably multicenter, comparative studies including both ruptured and intact AAAs.

title: Triple-Branched Stent-Grafts for Total Endovascular Repair of Aortic Arch Pathologies: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To summarize the early- and mid-term outcomes of triple-branched stent-grafts used for total endovascular repair of aortic arch pathologies. METHODS: A systematic literature search of PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, and Ovid Embase was conducted from January 1999 to May 2026 in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement. Reports describing human clinical experience with endovascular repair of aortic arch pathologies and reconstructing all 3 supra-aortic trunks were included. Single-branched or double-branched stent-graft or hybrid repair with open surgical debranching procedure were excluded. RESULTS: Seven studies with a total of 194 patients were included. The stent-grafts used for total endovascular arch repair comprised custom-made triple-branched stent-graft for the Zenith (Cook Medical), Relay (Terumo Aortic), and Inoue (PTMC Institute) platforms, the off-the-shelf Concave Supra-arch triple-branched stent-grafts (Lifetech Scientific), and a unibody device integrating one outer branch and 2 inner branches (MicroPort Scientific). Across eligible or separable data, technical success was 97.8% (n = 136/139), 30-day mortality 3.7% (n = 6/162), and stroke 6.2% (n = 10/162). No spinal cord ischemia or retrograde type A dissection was reported, and endoleak occurred in 18/100 patients (18.0%). Patency of the endovascularly reconstructed arch branches was 100% during follow-up. Branch stenosis occurred in 2.4% (4/168) of target vessels. Reintervention was performed in 26/155 patients (16.8%). CONCLUSION: Total endovascular aortic arch repair using a triple-branched endograft was feasible and safe with low rate of perioperative mortality and major complications in selected expert aortic centers. Neurologic complications, branch durability, endoleak, and reintervention remain major concerns during total endovascular arch repair.

title: An Integrated Inflammation-Metabolism Model for Stratifying Severity of Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) encompasses a spectrum ranging from asymptomatic disease and intermittent claudication to chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Inflammation and metabolic disturbance are increasingly recognized as interconnected features of atherosclerotic disease, but their combined relationship with CLTI status in PAD remains incompletely defined. This study investigated inflammation-metabolism interactions across molecular, population-level, and clinical datasets and developed a clinically applicable model for CLTI risk stratification among patients with PAD. METHODS: Public gene expression profiles were used to compare intermittent claudication with CLTI and healthy controls with PAD, focusing on inflammation-related and metabolism-related pathways. These molecular signals were then mapped to clinically measurable indices. The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data were used to evaluate associations between these indices and ankle-brachial index (ABI)-defined PAD at the population level; NHANES did not permit reliable subclassification of PAD severity. A separate single-center clinical cohort was used to compare controls, PAD without CLTI, and CLTI and to build a CLTI stratification model. Variables were selected by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and reintroduced into multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Inflammatory and metabolic pathways showed coordinated activation across disease-stage comparisons. In NHANES, the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic inflammation response index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) were associated with ABI-defined PAD in univariate analyses. In the clinical cohort, NLR, systemic immune-inflammation index, TyG, and AISI increased from controls to PAD without CLTI and CLTI (all P < 0.001), while qRT-PCR confirmed stepwise upregulation of key genes. Multivariable analysis identified high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), TyG, and AISI for PAD without CLTI, and BMI, smoking, hypertension, hs-CRP, and TyG for CLTI. The CLTI stratification model demonstrated good discrimination (area under the curve = 0.856). CONCLUSION: Inflammation-metabolism interactions are associated with PAD severity and CLTI status. Because the available data are cross-sectional, the model should be interpreted as a CLTI risk stratification tool rather than proof of longitudinal disease prediction. External prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Mitochondrial Omics in Macrophage Foam Cell Formation and Atherosclerosis.
abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of death worldwide, with atherosclerosis serving as the core pathological mechanism driving ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and peripheral artery disease. Macrophages play a central role in atherosclerosis by internalizing modified lipids and transforming them into foam cells, thereby driving plaque formation and progression. Mitochondrial metabolism is critically involved in regulating macrophage function, and targeting mitochondrial dysfunction may provide strategies for limiting plaque inflammation and improving plaque stability. Advances in high-throughput omics technologies and bioinformatic analysis methods have provided powerful tools for in-depth investigation of mitochondrial function. This review first summarizes macrophage heterogeneity and foam cell formation in atherosclerotic plaques. It then compares mitochondrial omics approaches, including proteomics, interactomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, isotope tracing, and emerging single-cell and spatial omics strategies. Finally, it discusses how mitochondrial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming contribute to macrophage foam cell formation, plaque inflammation, and atherosclerosis progression.

title: Carbon Dioxide Angiography as a Sole Contrast Modality in Endovascular Procedures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: 2 2 2 Iodinated contrast medium (ICM) carries risks of allergic reaction and post contrast acute kidney injury. Carbon dioxide (CO) angiography offers a potential alternative for patients with renal insufficiency or ICM allergy. Although extensive international studies have demonstrated the efficacy of COangiography, data on local populations remain limited. To provide region-specific data, we evaluated the accuracy and safety of COas the sole contrast modality in regional endovascular procedures. METHODS: 2 Clinical data of 28 patients who underwent various endovascular procedures using COangiography alone from April 2021 to December 2025 were retrospectively collected and analyzed. The primary end point was technical success. Secondary end points included postoperative renal function impairment and the incidence of complications. RESULTS: 2 2 The technical success rate for procedures performed with COangiography alone was 92.86% (26/28 cases). Serum creatinine (sCr) levels at 24 hours and 1 month postoperatively [112.85 μmol/L (interquartile range [IQR], 63.52-357.57) and 104.70 μmol/L (IQR, 65.35-356.62), respectively] showed no statistically significant difference compared to preoperative levels [105.55 μmol/L (IQR, 64.15-349.23)] (P > 0.05). In the 13 patients with preexisting renal insufficiency, mean sCr at 24 hours (358.70 ± 94.53 μmol/L) and 1 month (353.68 ± 90.10 μmol/L) also did not differ significantly from the preoperative mean (355.37 ± 91.64 μmol/L) (P > 0.05). Two patients undergoing renal artery stenting required adjunctive ICM (10 mL and 15 mL, respectively) due to suboptimal image quality. No CO-related complications occurred in any patient during or after the operation. CONCLUSION: 2 Within the constraints of a small retrospective design, COangiography appears to be a feasible and acceptably safe imaging alternative for specific endovascular procedures, particularly in patients with contraindications to ICM. These preliminary findings require confirmation through larger, prospective, multicenter investigations before broader clinical adoption can be recommended.

title: SWAM Mechanical Thrombectomy System Versus AngioJet Rheolytic Thrombectomy System for Acute Lower Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis: A Prospective, Randomized, Single-Center Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) poses a significant clinical burden due to its association with post-thrombotic syndrome and pulmonary embolism (PE). While the AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy system has established clinical utility, device-related hemolysis and embolic complications remain concerns. The Zhongtian SWAM (Synchronized Wave Aspiration and Maceration) system represents an innovative mechanical thrombectomy technology designed to minimize these adverse effects. OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical efficacy and safety profile of the Zhongtian SWAM mechanical thrombectomy system versus the AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy system in patients with acute lower extremity DVT in a prospective, randomized trial. METHODS: Between January 2022 and December 2024, 290 patients with acute lower extremity DVT (symptom duration ≤14 days) were randomized 1:1 to the SWAM group (n = 145) or the AngioJet group (n = 145). The primary endpoint was thrombus clearance grade (I-III) assessed by completion venography. Secondary endpoints included procedural time, urokinase dose, symptomatic PE incidence, hemolytic indices (plasma-free hemoglobin [PfHgb]), and 6-month primary patency. RESULTS: Grade III thrombus clearance was achieved in 78.6% of the SWAM patients versus 72.4% of the AngioJet patients (P = 0.221). Procedural time was significantly shorter in the SWAM group (42.3 ± 12.7 vs. 58.6 ± 15.4 min; P < 0.001). Urokinase consumption was markedly reduced in the SWAM group (150,000 ± 50,000 vs. 350,000 ± 100,000 IU; P < 0.001). Symptomatic PE occurred in 1.4% versus 5.5% of the patients (P = 0.048). Post-procedural PfHgb levels were substantially lower in the SWAM group (112.4 ± 45.3 vs. 438.7 ± 168.5 mg/dL; P < 0.001). Six-month primary patency was 91.0% versus 86.2% (P = 0.152). CONCLUSION: The Zhongtian SWAM system achieved comparable thrombus clearance to the AngioJet system with significantly shorter procedural time, reduced thrombolytic drug use, lower PE incidence, and markedly attenuated hemolysis. These findings support the SWAM system as a safe and effective alternative for percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy in acute lower extremity DVT.

title: Analysis of the Predictive Value of Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio for Long-Term Survival after Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Single-Center Retrospective Study and Propensity Score Matching Validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate factors influencing long-term survival in abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) patients following endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR), and analyze the predictive value of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on patients who underwent elective EVAR at our hospital between 2012 and 2021. Included patients had complete preoperative hematologic examinations, available postoperative follow-up data, and were excluded if they had symptomatic, infected/ruptured aneurysms, or an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class five. Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank test, Cox proportional hazards regression, Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and propensity score matching (PSM) were adopted for survival analysis, risk factor identification, optimal NLR cutoff determination, and confounding control, respectively. RESULTS: A study was conducted with a total of 537 participants, and 84% were male. During follow-up, 140 individuals (26%) died. Cox regression identified the following independent survival predictors: age (hazard ratio (HR), 1.060; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.038-1.081; P < 0.001), peripheral artery disease (PAD) (HR, 3.133; 95% CI, 1.629-6.025; P = 0.001), smoking (HR, 1.528; 95% CI, 1.010-2.311; P = 0.045), ASA classification (HR, 2.931; 95% CI, 1.906-4.507; P = 0.001), aneurysm diameter (HR, 1.181; 95% CI, 1.064-1.312; P = 0.002), and NLR (HR, 1.103; 95% CI, 1.061-1.147; P < 0.001). The NLR had an optimal cutoff value of 3.89 based on the ROC curve analysis. Patients in the high-NLR group had significantly lower overall survival time. This difference remained statistically significant after controlling for confounding variables through PSM (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Age, smoking, PAD, aneurysm diameter, ASA classification, and NLR are associated with long-term survival rates in AAA patients following EVAR. NLR holds significant value in post-EVAR prognostic assessment.

title: Early outcomes after acute type A aortic dissection repair: Adequate perfusion, rather than cannulation strategy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal arterial cannulation strategy for acute type A aortic dissection repair remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the association between cannulation strategy and early postoperative outcomes and to identify perioperative factors associated with adverse events. METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2019 and June 2024, including consecutive patients undergoing repair of acute type A aortic dissection. Primary outcomes were in-hospital death and postoperative neurologic complications. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity-score matching were used to evaluate associations with early outcomes. RESULTS: Among 866 patients, femoral, axillary, and combined femoral + axillary cannulation were used in 694 (80.1%), 144 (16.6%), and 28 (3.2%) patients, respectively. Patients in the axillary and combined groups more frequently had primary arch tears and underwent more extensive arch repair. In-hospital death occurred in 43 (5.0%) patients and postoperative neurologic complications in 113 (13.0%) patients, with comparable rates across groups; paraplegia was more frequent in the combined group (2/28 [7.1%]; P = .03). In multivariable analysis, axillary cannulation was not independently associated with in-hospital death (odds ratio, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 0.69-4.03), postoperative neurologic complications (odds ratio, 0.73; 95% confidence interval, 0.37-1.34), or cerebral infarction (odds ratio, 1.05; 95% confidence interval, 0.51-2.01). Preoperative shock (odds ratio, 3.20; 95% confidence interval, 1.44-6.91) and higher peak intraoperative lactate (odds ratio, 1.22; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-1.30) were independently associated with in-hospital death. In 142 propensity score-matched femoral-axillary pairs, mortality and neurologic complication rates remained similar. CONCLUSION: Cannulation strategy was not independently associated with in-hospital death or postoperative neurologic complications. Preoperative shock and higher peak intraoperative lactate were more consistently associated with adverse early outcomes, supporting the clinical importance of timely systemic reperfusion and effective cerebral protection.

title: Global Bacterial Spectrum, Diagnostic Culture Yield, and Microbiology-Related Mortality Risk in Infective Native Aortic Aneurysm: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysm (INAA) is a rare, fatal vascular infection, but its microbiology has been less synthesized than repair strategy. We assessed bacterial spectrum, culture yield, concurrent infectious foci, and microbiology-related mortality risk. METHODS: We systematically reviewed studies published to November 2024. The primary meta-analysis included 79 studies with 3,835 patients; 232 culture-confirmed case reports or small series (258 patients) were used only for descriptive pathogen mapping. Proportions were pooled with random-effects logit models, and hazard ratios (HRs) on the log-HR scale. RESULTS: The descriptive microbiology dataset included 4,093 patients, 2,609 with confirmed bacterial etiology. Salmonella was the leading genus globally (30.6%), followed by Staphylococcus (25.6%) and Streptococcus (11.8%). Staphylococcus predominated in developed countries (30.8%), whereas Salmonella dominated developing countries (59.0%) and China (60.6%). Any microbiological detection was achieved in 64.9% (95% CI, 60.1-69.4%; I2 = 82.0%). Blood culture, aortic tissue, preoperative, and intraoperative sampling positivity were 52.6%, 57.2%, 51.4%, and 61.4%, respectively. The most frequent concurrent foci were gastroenteritis (12.0%), spondylodiscitis (11.7%), urinary tract infection (8.6%), endocarditis (7.0%), and pneumonia (6.8%). Non-Salmonella-positive culture was associated with higher mortality (HR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.14-2.42); negative culture, Salmonella-positive culture, and positive blood culture were not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: INAA microbiology is geographically polarized, and culture yield remains incomplete across sampling strategies. These findings support region-aware empirical therapy, routine blood and tissue sampling with antibiotic-timing documentation, and pathogen-stratified registries and guidelines.

title: Clinical Efficacy of Different Endovascular Approaches in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease with Moderate-to-Severe Calcification: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To systematically evaluate the overall clinical outcomes of endovascular treatment in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) presenting with moderate-to-severe calcification of the femoropopliteal artery, and to descriptively summarize reported outcomes across different endovascular treatment strategies. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register, and Web of Science Core Collection from database inception to July 2026 to identify studies related to endovascular treatment in patients with moderate-to-severe calcified PAD of the femoropopliteal artery. The primary outcome measures included the 12-month primary patency rate and freedom from clinically driven target lesion revascularization (f-CD-TLR). RESULTS: A total of 13 studies were finally included. The overall analysis showed that the pooled effect size of the 12-month primary patency rate after endovascular treatment was 83.8%, and the pooled effect size of f-CD-TLR was 90.7%. Sensitivity analysis confirmed the high stability of the conclusions. Subgroup analyses, stratified by treatment strategy and presented in a neutral technology-based order, showed the following descriptive estimates: stent-based strategies (primary patency: 83.0%; f-CD-TLR: 87.12%), atherectomy-based strategies (86.66% and 96.58%), and intravascular lithotripsy-based strategies (82.75% and 89.2%). These subgroup estimates should be interpreted descriptively and should not be considered comparative rankings or evidence of superiority of one treatment strategy over another. No significant publication bias was detected; however, the reliability of these assessments may be limited in subgroups with a small number of studies. CONCLUSION: Endovascular treatment can achieve acceptable short-term outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe calcified femoropopliteal artery disease. Descriptive subgroup analyses demonstrated variation in reported outcomes across treatment strategies. Given the limited availability of head-to-head comparisons, further high-quality comparative studies between different devices are warranted to better define their relative efficacy.

title: Primary Aortic Mural Thrombus: Clinical Presentation, Embolization Patterns, and Early Outcomes in a Consecutive Series.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary aortic mural thrombus (PAMT) is an uncommon but clinically important source of systemic arterial embolization. This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, anatomical distribution, treatment strategies, and early outcomes of patients with PAMT. METHODS: Consecutive patients diagnosed with PAMT at a tertiary vascular center between January 2018 and December 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. PAMT was defined as an aortic mural thrombus diagnosed primarily on arterial phase computed tomography angiography in the absence of aortic aneurysm, dissection, or significant atherosclerotic disease. Clinical presentation, anatomic thrombus location, distal embolization territories, treatment strategy, follow-up imaging findings, recurrent embolization, repeat vascular intervention, and 90-day mortality were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: Twenty three patients were included. The median age was 56 years, and 20 patients were male. Acute lower limb ischemia was the most common presentation, occurring in 17 patients. Infrarenal abdominal aortic thrombus was the most frequent anatomic location, and the iliac arterial system was the most commonly involved embolization territory. Iliac and lower extremity embolization predominated among patients with infrarenal abdominal aortic thrombus, whereas visceral embolization was mainly observed in patients with suprarenal abdominal or multisegmental aortic thrombi. Endovascular aortic treatment was performed in 15 patients, open surgical aortic treatment was performed in three patients, and medical management of the aortic thrombus without direct aortic intervention was performed in five patients. The median follow-up duration was 3 months. During early follow-up, thrombus regression or resolution was observed in 18 patients, whereas persistent thrombus occurred in five patients. Recurrent embolization and repeat vascular intervention occurred in three patients each. The 90-day mortality rate was 8.7%. CONCLUSION: In this small retrospective consecutive series, PAMT most commonly presented with acute lower limb ischemia and was frequently located in the infrarenal abdominal aorta. Descriptive imaging analysis suggested that embolization territories may vary across anatomic thrombus locations, but this observation should be considered hypothesis-generating. Persistent thrombus and recurrent embolization occurred in a minority of patients during early follow-up. Standardized imaging assessment, etiologic evaluation, treatment reporting, and longer follow-up are needed to refine the management of PAMT.

title: Lesion Morphology-Guided Endovascular Treatment for Postthrombotic Iliofemoral Venous Obstruction: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular treatment of postthrombotic iliofemoral venous obstruction (PIVO) involves balloon angioplasty (percutaneous transluminal angioplasty [PTA]), stenting, or combined pharmacomechanical thrombectomy (PMT) with stenting, yet selection criteria remain poorly defined. This study evaluated outcomes of a lesion morphology-guided treatment allocation strategy. METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center cohort study (January 2019 to December 2023), 342 patients with confirmed PIVO (time since index deep vein thrombosis ≥3 months, Villalta score ≥5) treated at a tertiary vascular center were analyzed. Treatment was allocated based on lesion morphology: PTA alone for short-segment (<5 cm), nonocclusive lesions with good inflow (inflow score 0); stenting for long-segment (≥5 cm) or occlusive lesions with adequate inflow; and combined PMT/catheter-directed thrombolysis plus stenting for complex lesions with poor inflow (inflow score ≥2). The primary end point was 36-month primary patency. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 93.6%, 96.3%, and 94.0% of PTA, stenting, and combined procedures, respectively. At 36 months, primary patency was 51.3% (95% confidence interval [CI] 40.2-62.4) for PTA, 64.0% (95% CI 56.5-71.5) for stenting, and 57.0% (95% CI 46.8-67.2) for combined treatment (log-rank P = 0.041). The secondary patency was 65.4%, 80.5%, and 72.0%, respectively (P = 0.018). On multivariable Cox regression, stenting versus PTA was independently associated with reduced patency loss (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.89; P = 0.009), while inflow score ≥ 2 (HR 1.92, 95% CI 1.35-2.73; P < 0.001), complete occlusion (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.15-2.31; P = 0.006), and lesion length ≥10 cm (HR 1.56, 95% CI 1.12-2.18; P = 0.009) predicted patency loss. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, stenting remained superior to PTA (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.86; P = 0.007). Subgroup analysis showed stenting benefit was concentrated in long-segment lesions (≥5 cm; HR 0.42, P-int [P-value for interaction] = 0.003); for short, nonocclusive lesions, patency did not differ (HR 0.78, P = 0.43). CONCLUSION: A lesion morphology-guided treatment allocation strategy yields acceptable mid-term patency in PIVO. Stenting provides superior outcomes for long-segment and occlusive lesions, while PTA alone may be reasonable for carefully selected short-segment, nonocclusive stenoses with preserved inflow.

title: Conical Mesh-Disc Catheter-Directed Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Nationwide Prospective, Multicenter, Single-Arm Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Catheter-directed mechanical thrombectomy for acute pulmonary embolism (PE) has expanded rapidly, yet device-related pulmonary vascular injury has been reported with existing large-bore systems. We evaluated the feasibility and safety of a novel mechanical thrombectomy system incorporating conical nitinol mesh discs. METHODS: This nationwide prospective, single-arm, multicenter study enrolled adults with computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) confirmed acute PE, symptom duration ≤14 days, systolic blood pressure ≥90 mm Hg, and baseline right ventricular (RV) to left ventricle (LV) diameter ratio ≥0.9. The primary effectiveness endpoint was change in CTPA-derived RV/LV ratio from baseline to 48 hours. The primary safety endpoint was major adverse events (MAEs) within 48 hours. Secondary endpoints included changes in echocardiography-derived systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP) and oxygenation, as well as 30-day outcomes. RESULTS: Among 127 patients treated at 13 centers, device delivery, deployment, and removal were successful in all cases. RV/LV ratio decreased from 1.47 ± 0.37 to 0.83 ± 0.17 at 48 hours (95% CI: -0.69 to -0.59; P < 0.0001). Echocardiography-estimated sPAP decreased from 45.82 ± 14.46 to 36.66 ± 13.18 mm Hg (mean change: -9.69 ± 14.33; P < 0.001). Arterial oxygen partial pressure increased by 17.79 ± 15.50 mm Hg at 48 hours (P < 0.001) under standardized sampling conditions. No MAE occurred within 48 hours. No deaths or symptomatic recurrent PE occurred within 30 days. CONCLUSION: In hemodynamically stable patients with intermediate-risk acute PE and RV dilation, mechanical thrombectomy using a conical mesh-disc system was feasible and associated with early improvements in RV size and echocardiography-estimated pulmonary artery pressures, with no MAE observed within 48 hours. Given the single-arm design, comparative effectiveness versus anticoagulation or other devices cannot be inferred.

title: Outcomes of Symptom-Driven Top-Down versus Bottom-Up Strategies for Pelvic-Origin Extra-Pelvic Varicose Veins.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelvic-origin extra-pelvic varicose veins are increasingly recognized as a distinct phenotype of chronic venous disease. The optimal treatment sequence remains uncertain and is often selected according to the dominant clinical presentation. This study evaluated outcomes after symptom-driven top-down or bottom-up strategies in women with pelvic-origin extra-pelvic varicose veins. METHODS: We reviewed consecutive women with pelvic-origin extra-pelvic varicose veins treated between 2018 and 2024. Diagnosis was based on clinical examination, duplex ultrasound, and pelvic venous imaging. Patients with clinically relevant pelvic symptoms were generally treated with a top-down strategy, whereas patients with predominantly extra-pelvic manifestations and no significant pelvic symptoms were treated with a bottom-up strategy. Extra-pelvic outcomes were assessed using the revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), the Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire-20 (CIVIQ-20), technical success, escape point occlusion, and recurrence-free survival. Pelvic pain response in the top-down group was assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS) and parauterine vein diameter. RESULTS: Seventy-five patients were included: 32 in the top-down group and 43 in the bottom-up group. The groups had similar baseline characteristics, except for age (bottom-up group was older). At 3 months, no statistically significant differences were observed in rVCSS and CIVIQ-20 scores between the selected treatment groups (P = 0.71 and P = 0.86, respectively). Escape point occlusion rates were 93.8% and 97.7% (P = 0.58), lower limb symptom resolution rates were 100% and 95.3% (P = 0.24), and vulvar varices resolution rates were 87.5% and 93.0% (P = 0.47), respectively. At 3-year follow-up, the recurrence rate was 6.25% in the top-down group and 11.6% in the bottom-up group. Recurrence-free survival rates at 5 years were not statistically different between the groups (log-rank P = 0.33). Cox regression analysis identified BMI as a significant predictor of recurrence (HR = 2.654, P = 0.015). CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort of clinically selected patients, symptom-driven top-down and bottom-up strategies were both associated with favorable short-term outcomes and mid-term durability. Because the two groups represented different clinical phenotypes rather than randomized comparable populations, these findings should not be interpreted as proof of equivalent effectiveness. Treatment selection should be individualized based on pelvic symptoms, pelvic hemodynamics, and extra-pelvic anatomical patterns.

title: Twelve-Month Amputation-Free Survival after AngioJet Thrombectomy for Acute and Subacute Lower Extremity Arterial Thrombosis: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the 12-month efficacy and safety of AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy in patients with acute and subacute lower extremity arterial thrombosis. METHODS: This was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm cohort study (NCT04861506) conducted at 7 tertiary centers in China. A total of 203 consecutive patients with acute/subacute limb ischemia (Rutherford I-IIb) underwent AngioJet pharmacomechanical thrombectomy between February 2021 and May 2023. The primary end points were 12-month amputation-free survival (AFS) and VascuQoL scores. The secondary end points included technical success, thrombus removal grade, perioperative complications, and freedom from major adverse events (MAEs). RESULTS: Device safety was 100%, and technical success was 97.5% (198/203). Complete thrombus removal (grade 0) was achieved in 79.8% (162/203). At 12 months, AFS was 92.1% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 87.4-95.0%), and freedom from MAEs was 79.8% (95% CI: 74.9-86.0%). VascuQoL scores improved from 2.43 ± 1.28 to 4.76 ± 1.21 (P < 0.001). Perioperative complications occurred in 22.2% of patients, with major complications occurring in 6.9%. Complete thrombus removal, tibial runoff score ≤5, and postoperative anticoagulation were independent predictors of limb salvage (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: AngioJet thrombectomy provides high technical success and durable 12-month limb salvage with acceptable safety in acute and subacute lower extremity arterial thrombosis. Complete thrombus removal, favorable runoff, and postoperative anticoagulation are key prognostic factors.

title: Uric Acid-To-High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Ratio and Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To examine the association between the serum uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) ratio (UHR) and peripheral arterial disease (PAD) among U.S. adults. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 1999 to 2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). PAD was defined as ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.90 in either leg. Weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) for PAD according to UHR modeled continuously and by quartiles. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression, subgroup analyses, interaction tests, sensitivity analyses, stratified receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses, and propensity score matching (PSM) were performed. RESULTS: A total of 6,149 participants were included, among whom 459 had PAD (7.5%). Each one-unit increase in UHR was associated with higher odds of PAD (OR, 1.04, P = 0.004). The highest UHR quartile (≥14.47) was associated with 52% higher odds of PAD compared with the lowest quartile (<7.78) (P = 0.036). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P for overall = 0.006) without evidence of a statistically significant nonlinear pattern (P for nonlinearity = 0.375). Stratified ROC analysis identified optimal cut-offs of 10.69 for the overall population (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.577), 12.55 for statin users (AUC = 0.602), and 9.82 for nonstatin users (AUC = 0.554). PSM confirmed the overall association (P = 0.027), with significance retained only among statin users (P = 0.002). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses generally supported the robustness of the findings. CONCLUSION: Higher UHR is independently associated with PAD. UHR may serve as an adjunctive screening marker, particularly for statin users (cut-off ≥12.55).

title: Chronic Kidney Disease as an Independent Risk Factor for Chronic Lower Extremity Ulcers: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of US Adults.
abstract: BackgroundChronic lower extremity ulcers (CLEU) are a significant health burden, often linked to complications such as diabetes and vascular diseases. Chronic kidney disease (CKD), a prevalent global health issue, has been increasingly associated with CLEU, though the nature of this relationship remains poorly understood. This study aimed to explore the association between CKD and CLEU in the US adult population.MethodsWe analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) between 1999 and 2004. The study included adults aged 20 years and older who completed interviews and examinations. CLEU was defined as self-reported ulcers or sores on the leg or foot lasting more than four weeks. CKD was diagnosed based on the 2012 KDIGO guidelines, using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR). Logistic regression models were used to assess the association between CKD and CLEU, adjusting for demographics, BMI, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities.ResultsAmong 8564 participants, individuals with CKD had a higher likelihood of developing CLEU, with an unadjusted odds ratio (OR) of 2.33 (95% CI: 1.86-2.91). After adjusting for confounders, the association remained significant, with adjusted ORs of 1.64 (95% CI: 1.26-2.12) and 1.57 (95% CI: 1.2-2.04) in Models 2 and 3, respectively. Stratified analyses showed no significant interactions across subgroups defined by age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral artery disease (PAD).ConclusionThis study demonstrates a robust association between CKD and CLEU in US adults, suggesting that CKD is an independent risk factor for CLEU. These findings highlight the need for integrated management strategies for CKD patients to reduce the risk of CLEU. Future longitudinal studies are needed to establish causality and inform targeted interventions.
